title: Torricelli and the Puy de Dome
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Stand up a mercury column, swap the liquid for water and watch it need a ten-metre tube, then carry a barometer up a mountain and see which of two rival hypotheses survives.

educational.topic: Torricelli and the Puy de Dome
learningObjectives: Explain why a mercury column stands at a particular height.
Predict how that height changes with altitude and with the density of the liquid.
Explain how the Puy de Dome result ruled out the competing hypothesis.
prerequisites: Knowing that density is mass per unit volume
Chapter 7 sections on what pressure is

keyQuestions: Why did Torricelli use mercury rather than water?
What was at the top of the tube, and why was that controversial?
Why did Perier leave a second barometer at the bottom of the mountain?
commonMisconceptions: Believing something inside the tube holds the liquid up.
Thinking the column height depends on the width of the tube.
Assuming a vacuum sucks, rather than that the air outside pushes.
assessmentOpportunities: Explains the column height as a balance between the weight of the liquid and the pressure of the air.
Predicts the direction and rough size of the change with altitude before measuring.
States what the Puy de Dome result ruled out, not only what it showed.
